newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends mostly down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends mostly down on profit-taking.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mostly down on Thursday on institutional profit-taking at higher levels, traders said.

The most actively traded November 1997 contract ended at 20,900 yuan ($2,521) per tonne, losing 100 yuan. It opened at 20,810 yuan, hitting an intraday low of 20,800 and a high of 21,260 yuan per tonne.
August fell 100 to 20,600 yuan, September was unchanged at 20,800, October dropped 100 to 20,900, December 100 to 20,900, and the January 1997 contract 100 to 20,900 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume rose to 94,160 tonnes from 74,080 tonnes.
Copper opened lower and moved in a wide range for most of the session.

Traders said overnight losses on the London Metal Exchange (LME) rattled the confidence of long position holders, who took profits when prices were pushed to higher levels by some speculative buying in mid-morning trade.
"Many investors cashed out at higher levels today due to overnight LME losses but buying was still active at around the 20,800-yuan level," one trader said.
"Investors are mixed about which way the market will go from here, resulting in fluctuations late in the session," he added.
LME copper ended down $27 a tonne on Wednesday at $2,273.
Analysts in London said that rising stocks, contracting nearby backwardations and downtrending chart signals were likely to see LME copper favour further losses on Thursday.
LME copper stocks moved up 3,950 tonnes.
In Shanghai, physical copper prices were around 20,700 yuan, up from the 22,550-yuan level at the opening session due to gains on the futures market late in the session.
Traders said spot copper demand remained dull but futures were likely to get support from institutional buyers, and this could see red metal futures move in a wide range in the short term.
"Sharp falls seem impossible due to a lack of market-moving news," a second trader said.
"If the institutional support pushes prices up, copper will meet strong resistance above the 21,000-yuan level," he said.
Traders said they expected copper to consolidate around current levels on Friday.
Aluminium ended up.
August rose 240 to 14,090 yuan per tonne, September 230 to 14,320, October 280 to 14,400, November 330 to 14,380, the first traded December 1997 contract ended at 14,470 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume rose to 4,760 tonnes from 3,730 tonnes.
